title: Extension by zero preserves constructibility and Tor amplitude
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ be an
open immersion of
finite-type $k$-schemes, and use the
finite coefficient ring $A$.
For a bounded
constructible complex $K$ of
finite Tor amplitude, its
extension by zero
$j_!K$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Its
cohomological range
and Tor amplitude may be taken to be those of $K$.

proof.text: Let F be the recorded exact intrinsic extension by zero. The exact-functor homology isomorphism gives H^r(D(F)K) = F(H^r K). Since F preserves zero objects, every supplied cohomological interval is preserved. The set of nonzero homology degrees of D(F)K is a subset of that of K, hence finite.

Finite type over the field k makes Y locally Noetherian, hence the open immersion j is quasi-compact. Restriction to constant scalars identifies intrinsic constructibility with fixed-module constructibility. The canonical realization followed by restriction is naturally the identity, so the inverse realization of a constructible intrinsic sheaf is constructible as well.

A constructible fixed-module pro-etale sheaf has a constructible etale origin G. Quasi-compact open extension by zero preserves etale constructibility by lem-fin-extension-by-zero, whose proof extends the strata and adjoins the closed complement. The natural comparison nu^* j_! G = j_! nu^* G transfers this to fixed-module pro-etale extension. Transfer through the canonical realization and the homology isomorphism of step 1 proves intrinsic constructibility of every homology sheaf of D(F)K. Together with finite support this proves bounded constructibility.

The cardinality of k_0 gives characteristic p, so the distinct prime l is a unit in k_0 and then in k. The map from k through global sections to each residue field supplies invertibility on U and Y. For each given Tor interval [a,b], lem-sf-flat-model gives a flat complex P supported in [a,b] and isomorphic to K. Use the reduced closed complement of j and the extension clause of lem-sfb-open-closed-flatness: every term of F(P) is flat. Additivity preserves its zero terms outside [a,b]. The exact derived-functor factorization identifies D(F)K with Q(F(P)). Apply lem-sf-flat-model in the reverse direction using bounded constructibility from step 3. This proves the original Tor interval; applying it to the finite-Tor witness and combining with bounded constructibility proves membership in D^b_ctf.
